raw_findings.body: Deleting a client throws UnsupportedOperationException inside the provider event listener, failing/rolling back the client removal operation with a server error whenever both feature flags are active.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Runtime UnsupportedOperationException aborts client removal when both features are enabled.
raw_findings.impact: Deleting a client throws UnsupportedOperationException inside the provider event listener, failing/rolling back the client removal operation with a server error whenever both feature flags are active.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new feature gate checks only Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ while the newly overridden MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() now returns ClientPermissionsV2, whose setPermissionsEnabled is unsupported.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Gate the listener on V1 being enabled AND V2 being disabled (or dispatch to the V1 MgmtPermissions implementation explicitly instead of the feature-selecting management() factory).
raw_findings.title: Client deletion fails with UnsupportedOperationException when V1 and V2 FGAP features are both enabled
raw_findings.trigger: Both ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) and ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 profile features are enabled and any client is deleted, firing ClientModel.ClientRemovedEvent. The listener gate only checks the V1 flag, but management() prefers V2 and returns MgmtPermissionsV2, whose new clients() override returns ClientPermissionsV2 where setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2").

raw_findings.body: Orphaned authorization resources and scope permissions referencing the deleted client's UUID remain in the admin-permissions resource server, polluting permission listings and evaluation with stale entries that can never be resolved to a client.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Stale resource/permission rows accumulate after client deletion, corrupting FGAP-V2 permission data.
raw_findings.impact: Orphaned authorization resources and scope permissions referencing the deleted client's UUID remain in the admin-permissions resource server, polluting permission listings and evaluation with stale entries that can never be resolved to a client.
raw_findings.root_cause: The patch introduces per-client V2 resources but restricts the removal-event cleanup listener to the V1 feature without adding an equivalent V2 cleanup.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add a V2 branch in the removal listener (or a dedicated synchronizer) that deletes the resource named by the removed client's id and its associated permissions in the admin-permissions resource server.
raw_findings.title: V2 FGAP client resources and permissions are never cleaned up when the underlying client is deleted
raw_findings.trigger: With only ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 enabled, an admin creates a per-client scope permission (which creates a Resource named by the client UUID via AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource) and then the client is deleted; the removal listener is now skipped entirely because it is gated on the V1 flag, and no V2 cleanup path exists.

raw_findings.body: The method never returns the ids of individually granted clients, and if the umbrella all-clients permission is granted it adds the literal string "Clients" to a set that callers interpret as client ids, breaking client-list filtering for restricted admins.
raw_findings.failure_mode: getClientsWithPermission returns an empty set or the bogus entry "Clients" instead of granted client ids.
raw_findings.impact: The method never returns the ids of individually granted clients, and if the umbrella all-clients permission is granted it adds the literal string "Clients" to a set that callers interpret as client ids, breaking client-list filtering for restricted admins.
raw_findings.root_cause: Mismatch between the lookup key (resource type "Clients") and per-client resources that are created without a type by the schema's getOrCreateResource.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Set the resource type to CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE when creating per-client resources in AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource (and exclude the umbrella type resource from the result), or enumerate per-client resources by another criterion.
raw_findings.title: getClientsWithPermission queries by resource type that per-client resources never have, returning wrong results
raw_findings.trigger: getClientsWithPermission is called after per-client permissions were created: AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource creates per-client resources via resourceStore.create(...) without ever calling setType, so findByType(server, "Clients") matches only the umbrella "Clients" resource created in init() (which does set the type), never the per-client resources.

raw_findings.body: Permission evaluation for a client without a per-client resource throws a NullPointerException, turning admin REST requests into 500 errors instead of a clean permission denial.
raw_findings.failure_mode: NullPointerException during permission evaluation instead of returning false.
raw_findings.impact: Permission evaluation for a client without a per-client resource throws a NullPointerException, turning admin REST requests into 500 errors instead of a clean permission denial.
raw_findings.root_cause: Missing null check on the umbrella resource returned by getResourceTypeResource before it is passed to policyStore.findByResource.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Return false when getResourceTypeResource yields null before calling policyStore.findByResource, mirroring the null guard used for the per-client resource.
raw_findings.title: NPE in hasPermission when the "Clients" type resource does not exist on the resource server
raw_findings.trigger: An admin-permissions resource server that was initialized before this patch (upgrade scenario) contains only the "Users" resource, or supportsAuthorizationSchema returns false (e.g., realm's admin-permissions flag toggled off while the client still exists); getResourceTypeResource then returns null and findByResource(server, null) dereferences the null resource.

raw_findings.body: Misleading API documentation: callers may expect a boolean result rather than an exception-throwing guard, unlike the sibling require* methods that are correctly documented as throwing ForbiddenException.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Documentation contradicts the method's actual contract.
raw_findings.impact: Misleading API documentation: callers may expect a boolean result rather than an exception-throwing guard, unlike the sibling require* methods that are correctly documented as throwing ForbiddenException.
raw_findings.root_cause: Copy-paste of a can*-style Javadoc onto a void require* guard method.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Change the Javadoc to "Throws ForbiddenException if {@link #canView()} returns {@code false}."
raw_findings.title: Javadoc for requireView() incorrectly documents it as returning a boolean
raw_findings.trigger: A developer reads the newly added Javadoc for the void method requireView(), which claims the method "Returns true" although it returns nothing and instead throws ForbiddenException when canView() is false.

raw_findings.body: Misleading API documentation for the guard method, inconsistent with the other require* methods documented as throwing ForbiddenException.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Documentation contradicts the method's actual contract.
raw_findings.impact: Misleading API documentation for the guard method, inconsistent with the other require* methods documented as throwing ForbiddenException.

raw_findings.suggested_fix: Change the Javadoc to "Throws ForbiddenException if {@link #canViewClientScopes()} returns {@code false}."
raw_findings.title: Javadoc for requireViewClientScopes() incorrectly documents it as returning a boolean
raw_findings.trigger: A developer reads the newly added Javadoc for the void method requireViewClientScopes(), which claims it "Returns true" even though the method is void and throws ForbiddenException when canViewClientScopes() is false.

raw_findings.body: Any current or future code in MgmtPermissions that reads the protected clientPermissions field directly will see null (or a stale V1 instance) instead of the cached V2 evaluator, a latent inconsistency and a maintainability trap; the sibling userPermissions field avoids shadowing by using a distinct name.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Field shadowing creates two divergent caches for the same evaluator.
raw_findings.impact: Any current or future code in MgmtPermissions that reads the protected clientPermissions field directly will see null (or a stale V1 instance) instead of the cached V2 evaluator, a latent inconsistency and a maintainability trap; the sibling userPermissions field avoids shadowing by using a distinct name.
raw_findings.root_cause: New subclass field declared with the same name as an inherited protected field.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Reuse the inherited protected clientPermissions field in the clients() override (casting as needed) or rename the new field so it does not shadow the parent field.
raw_findings.title: MgmtPermissionsV2.clientPermissions shadows the inherited protected field of the same name
raw_findings.trigger: MgmtPermissions already declares 'protected ClientPermissions clientPermissions'; the new private field in the subclass shadows it, so the parent field stays null while the child field holds the V2 instance whenever the V2 evaluator is used.

raw_findings.body: Dead code and its supporting imports (plus the unused logger field and TOKEN_EXCHANGE static import) add maintenance noise and compiler warnings, and suggest an unfinished token-exchange implementation to future readers.
raw_findings.evidence: private EvaluationContext getEvaluationContext(ClientModel authorizedClient, AccessToken token) {
raw_findings.failure_mode: Unreachable private method ships in production code.
raw_findings.impact: Dead code and its supporting imports (plus the unused logger field and TOKEN_EXCHANGE static import) add maintenance noise and compiler warnings, and suggest an unfinished token-exchange implementation to future readers.
raw_findings.root_cause: Copied V1 helper retained in the new V2 class while the feature that used it is unsupported.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Remove getEvaluationContext together with the unused logger field and unused imports, or wire it into an actual V2 token-exchange implementation.
raw_findings.title: Dead private method getEvaluationContext in ClientPermissionsV2 is never called
raw_findings.trigger: The new class defines getEvaluationContext (and the ClientModelIdentity/DefaultEvaluationContext imports it needs), but the only conceivable caller, canExchangeTo, throws UnsupportedOperationException, so the method is unreachable dead code.

raw_findings.body: Token-exchange requests that previously received a clean permission denial now surface as an unhandled UnsupportedOperationException (HTTP 500), because canExchangeTo's callers are gated by the token-exchange feature, not by the V1 FGAP feature.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Runtime exception on a reachable evaluation path when feature flags are combined.
raw_findings.impact: Token-exchange requests that previously received a clean permission denial now surface as an unhandled UnsupportedOperationException (HTTP 500), because canExchangeTo's callers are gated by the token-exchange feature, not by the V1 FGAP feature.
raw_findings.root_cause: A boolean permission check reachable from non-V1-gated code paths was replaced by an unconditional UnsupportedOperationException.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Return false (deny) from canExchangeTo in V2, or verify every call site is unreachable when V2 is enabled and document that invariant.
raw_findings.title: Legacy token exchange throws UnsupportedOperationException instead of denying when V2 FGAP is enabled
raw_findings.trigger: The legacy token-exchange flow calls AdminPermissions.management(...).clients().canExchangeTo(...); if the token-exchange feature and ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 are enabled together, management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2 and this override throws instead of returning false.

raw_findings.body: A regression in the map-roles-client-scope evaluation path (e.g., wrong scope name or broken fallback to the all-clients resource) would ship undetected because the new authorization branch is untested.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Untested authorization branch allows silent regressions in a security-relevant check.
raw_findings.impact: A regression in the map-roles-client-scope evaluation path (e.g., wrong scope name or broken fallback to the all-clients resource) would ship undetected because the new authorization branch is untested.
raw_findings.root_cause: New scope and evaluator method added without a corresponding integration test, unlike the other client scopes covered in the new test class.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Extend PermissionClientTest with a case that grants Set.of(MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE) on a client and verifies scope-mapping role operations succeed only after the grant.
raw_findings.title: New MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE client scope has no end-to-end test coverage
raw_findings.trigger: PermissionClientTest exercises MANAGE, CONFIGURE, VIEW, MAP_ROLES and MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE, but no test grants or evaluates the newly added map-roles-client-scope scope via canMapClientScopeRoles.

raw_findings.title: Unused `java.util.Arrays` import left behind after removing its only usage

raw_findings.body: The round-trip through the builder is dead code that obscures intent and misleads readers into thinking a representation is needed, adding needless object construction in a hot test path.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Redundant, confusing expression survives the refactor, reducing test readability and maintainability.

finding.body: Any current or future code in MgmtPermissions that reads the protected clientPermissions field directly will see null (or a stale V1 instance) instead of the cached V2 evaluator, a latent inconsistency and a maintainability trap; the sibling userPermissions field avoids shadowing by using a distinct name.

finding.root_cause: New subclass field declared with the same name as an inherited protected field.
finding.suggested_fix: Reuse the inherited protected clientPermissions field in the clients() override (casting as needed) or rename the new field so it does not shadow the parent field.
finding.title: MgmtPermissionsV2.clientPermissions shadows the inherited protected field of the same name

finding.body: Token-exchange requests that previously received a clean permission denial now surface as an unhandled UnsupportedOperationException (HTTP 500), because canExchangeTo's callers are gated by the token-exchange feature, not by the V1 FGAP feature.
finding.failure_mode: Runtime exception on a reachable evaluation path when feature flags are combined.

finding.root_cause: A boolean permission check reachable from non-V1-gated code paths was replaced by an unconditional UnsupportedOperationException.
finding.suggested_fix: Return false (deny) from canExchangeTo in V2, or verify every call site is unreachable when V2 is enabled and document that invariant.
finding.title: Legacy token exchange throws UnsupportedOperationException instead of denying when V2 FGAP is enabled
finding.trigger: The legacy token-exchange flow calls AdminPermissions.management(...).clients().canExchangeTo(...); if the token-exchange feature and ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 are enabled together, management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2 and this override throws instead of returning false.
finding.verifier_reason: The finding claims canExchangeTo is reachable when V2 is enabled. If V2 is enabled without V1, token exchange features wouldn't be enabled. The trigger scenario combining token-exchange with V2-only is unproven.

validated_findings.body: Deleting a client throws UnsupportedOperationException inside the provider event listener, failing/rolling back the client removal operation with a server error whenever both feature flags are active.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Runtime UnsupportedOperationException aborts client removal when both features are enabled.
validated_findings.impact: Deleting a client throws UnsupportedOperationException inside the provider event listener, failing/rolling back the client removal operation with a server error whenever both feature flags are active.
validated_findings.root_cause: The new feature gate checks only Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ while the newly overridden MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() now returns ClientPermissionsV2, whose setPermissionsEnabled is unsupported.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Gate the listener on V1 being enabled AND V2 being disabled (or dispatch to the V1 MgmtPermissions implementation explicitly instead of the feature-selecting management() factory).
validated_findings.title: Client deletion fails with UnsupportedOperationException when V1 and V2 FGAP features are both enabled
validated_findings.trigger: Both ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) and ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 profile features are enabled and any client is deleted, firing ClientModel.ClientRemovedEvent. The listener gate only checks the V1 flag, but management() prefers V2 and returns MgmtPermissionsV2, whose new clients() override returns ClientPermissionsV2 where setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2").
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The patch gates the listener on V1 only (line 77), but management() at line 66-70 returns MgmtPermissionsV2 when V2 is enabled. However, the claim that both V1 and V2 can be enabled simultaneously is unsubstantiated - Profile.Feature shows V1 and V2 are separate versioned features. The code path only enters when V1 is enabled (line 77), and in that case management() would return MgmtPermissions (V1), not MgmtPermissionsV2. The trigger scenario requires both features enabled simultaneously which is not proven possible.

validated_findings.body: Orphaned authorization resources and scope permissions referencing the deleted client's UUID remain in the admin-permissions resource server, polluting permission listings and evaluation with stale entries that can never be resolved to a client.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Stale resource/permission rows accumulate after client deletion, corrupting FGAP-V2 permission data.
validated_findings.impact: Orphaned authorization resources and scope permissions referencing the deleted client's UUID remain in the admin-permissions resource server, polluting permission listings and evaluation with stale entries that can never be resolved to a client.
validated_findings.root_cause: The patch introduces per-client V2 resources but restricts the removal-event cleanup listener to the V1 feature without adding an equivalent V2 cleanup.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Add a V2 branch in the removal listener (or a dedicated synchronizer) that deletes the resource named by the removed client's id and its associated permissions in the admin-permissions resource server.
validated_findings.title: V2 FGAP client resources and permissions are never cleaned up when the underlying client is deleted
validated_findings.trigger: With only ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 enabled, an admin creates a per-client scope permission (which creates a Resource named by the client UUID via AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource) and then the client is deleted; the removal listener is now skipped entirely because it is gated on the V1 flag, and no V2 cleanup path exists.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The claim that V2 cleanup is missing assumes V2 creates per-client resources that need cleanup. However, the listener is gated on V1 (line 77), and when only V2 is enabled, the listener block is skipped entirely. The finding assumes V2 creates resources via AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource, but there's no evidence this creates orphaned data requiring cleanup - the schema may handle this differently. Speculative without proof of actual orphan creation.

validated_findings.body: The method never returns the ids of individually granted clients, and if the umbrella all-clients permission is granted it adds the literal string "Clients" to a set that callers interpret as client ids, breaking client-list filtering for restricted admins.
validated_findings.failure_mode: getClientsWithPermission returns an empty set or the bogus entry "Clients" instead of granted client ids.
validated_findings.impact: The method never returns the ids of individually granted clients, and if the umbrella all-clients permission is granted it adds the literal string "Clients" to a set that callers interpret as client ids, breaking client-list filtering for restricted admins.
validated_findings.root_cause: Mismatch between the lookup key (resource type "Clients") and per-client resources that are created without a type by the schema's getOrCreateResource.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Set the resource type to CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE when creating per-client resources in AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource (and exclude the umbrella type resource from the result), or enumerate per-client resources by another criterion.
validated_findings.title: getClientsWithPermission queries by resource type that per-client resources never have, returning wrong results
validated_findings.trigger: getClientsWithPermission is called after per-client permissions were created: AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource creates per-client resources via resourceStore.create(...) without ever calling setType, so findByType(server, "Clients") matches only the umbrella "Clients" resource created in init() (which does set the type), never the per-client resources.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The claim that per-client resources are created without a type is speculative. Looking at AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource (lines 76-114), resources are created via resourceStore.create() and then updateScopes is called, but the code does set scopes from the resource type. The finding assumes findByType won't match, but the umbrella 'Clients' resource created in init() would be found. The actual behavior depends on how resources are created elsewhere, which isn't proven to be typeless.

validated_findings.body: Permission evaluation for a client without a per-client resource throws a NullPointerException, turning admin REST requests into 500 errors instead of a clean permission denial.
validated_findings.failure_mode: NullPointerException during permission evaluation instead of returning false.
validated_findings.impact: Permission evaluation for a client without a per-client resource throws a NullPointerException, turning admin REST requests into 500 errors instead of a clean permission denial.
validated_findings.root_cause: Missing null check on the umbrella resource returned by getResourceTypeResource before it is passed to policyStore.findByResource.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Return false when getResourceTypeResource yields null before calling policyStore.findByResource, mirroring the null guard used for the per-client resource.
validated_findings.title: NPE in hasPermission when the "Clients" type resource does not exist on the resource server
validated_findings.trigger: An admin-permissions resource server that was initialized before this patch (upgrade scenario) contains only the "Users" resource, or supportsAuthorizationSchema returns false (e.g., realm's admin-permissions flag toggled off while the client still exists); getResourceTypeResource then returns null and findByResource(server, null) dereferences the null resource.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The claim assumes getResourceTypeResource returns null in upgrade scenarios. However, looking at AdminPermissionsSchema.getResourceTypeResource (lines 116-134), it returns null only if supportsAuthorizationSchema returns false or resourceType is null. The finding's trigger scenario (upgrade with only Users resource) is speculative - there's no evidence the Clients resource wouldn't exist after proper initialization. The null check concern is valid but the trigger is unproven.

validated_findings.impact: A regression in the map-roles-client-scope evaluation path (e.g., wrong scope name or broken fallback to the all-clients resource) would ship undetected because the new authorization branch is untested.
validated_findings.root_cause: New scope and evaluator method added without a corresponding integration test, unlike the other client scopes covered in the new test class.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Extend PermissionClientTest with a case that grants Set.of(MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE) on a client and verifies scope-mapping role operations succeed only after the grant.
validated_findings.title: New MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE client scope has no end-to-end test coverage
validated_findings.trigger: PermissionClientTest exercises MANAGE, CONFIGURE, VIEW, MAP_ROLES and MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE, but no test grants or evaluates the newly added map-roles-client-scope scope via canMapClientScopeRoles.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: This is a test coverage gap claim. While canMapClientScopeRoles exists at line 100-103, the absence of a specific test is a test gap observation, not a defect in the code itself. The method implementation follows the same pattern as other tested methods. Test gaps are outside the scope of code defects.

validated_findings.body: The file now carries a dead `java.util.Arrays` import; in Keycloak's build, unused imports are flagged by static-analysis/checkstyle rules, causing verification failures or lint noise for a file this patch otherwise cleaned up (it correctly removed the `Collectors` import for the same reason).
validated_findings.failure_mode: Stale import survives the refactor, tripping unused-import lint checks and degrading code hygiene.
validated_findings.impact: The file now carries a dead `java.util.Arrays` import; in Keycloak's build, unused imports are flagged by static-analysis/checkstyle rules, causing verification failures or lint noise for a file this patch otherwise cleaned up (it correctly removed the `Collectors` import for the same reason).
validated_findings.root_cause: The patch deleted the private createUserPermission helper (the sole consumer of Arrays) without pruning the corresponding import.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Also remove `import java.util.Arrays;` from UserResourceTypeEvaluationTest, mirroring the removal of `import java.util.stream.Collectors;`.
validated_findings.title: Unused `java.util.Arrays` import left behind after removing its only usage
validated_findings.trigger: Compiling the test module or running the project's checkstyle/import-order verification after this patch removes the only `Arrays` usage in the file (the deleted createUserPermission helper) while retaining `import java.util.Arrays;` at the top of the file.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The finding claims unused Arrays import on LEFT side (line 411 shows deleted code using Arrays.asList). However, the patch shows this is on the LEFT/deleted side - the code was removed. The finding incorrectly claims the import survives; if the usage was deleted, the import would also need removal, but this is about the old code being deleted, not new code being added with stale imports.

validated_findings.body: Inconsistent formatting across eleven newly added call sites in the same file violates the codebase's uniform argument-spacing convention, producing avoidable diff noise and failing auto-format checks if enforced.
validated_findings.evidence: UserPolicyRepresentation policy = createUserPolicy(realm, client,"Only My Admin User Policy", realm.admin().users().search("myadmin").get(0).getId());
validated_findings.failure_mode: Formatting inconsistency is introduced across a repeated pattern of new lines, degrading maintainability and reviewer signal.
validated_findings.impact: Inconsistent formatting across eleven newly added call sites in the same file violates the codebase's uniform argument-spacing convention, producing avoidable diff noise and failing auto-format checks if enforced.
validated_findings.root_cause: Mechanical insertion of the new `realm, client` parameters during the refactor omitted the space before the string literal at most call sites.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Insert the missing space after `client,` in all affected `createUserPolicy(realm, client,"…")` calls to match `createUserPolicy(realm, client, "…")`.
validated_findings.title: Missing space after argument in repeated `createUserPolicy(realm, client,"…")` calls
validated_findings.trigger: Any reviewer or formatter pass over the newly added calls at R103, R143, R157, R190, R205, R208, R218, R221, R245, R295, and R335, which all omit the space after `client,`, unlike R84 in the same file and every call site in PermissionClientTest which use `createUserPolicy(realm, client, "…")`.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 103 shows 'createUserPolicy(realm, client,"Only My Admin User Policy"' - missing space after 'client,'. Comparing to line 84 which shows 'createUserPolicy(realm, client, "Only My Admin User Policy"' with proper spacing. This is an inconsistent formatting pattern across multiple call sites in the same file.

validated_findings.body: The round-trip through the builder is dead code that obscures intent and misleads readers into thinking a representation is needed, adding needless object construction in a hot test path.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Redundant, confusing expression survives the refactor, reducing test readability and maintainability.
validated_findings.impact: The round-trip through the builder is dead code that obscures intent and misleads readers into thinking a representation is needed, adding needless object construction in a hot test path.
validated_findings.root_cause: During the migration from the representation-based helper to the id-based `createPermission(client, resourceId, …)` signature, the old builder expression was kept and `.getId()` appended instead of passing the existing id.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Replace the argument with `newUserId` directly: `createPermission(client, newUserId, usersType, Set.of(MANAGE), policy);`.
validated_findings.title: Pointless `UserConfigBuilder.create().id(newUserId).build().getId()` instead of using `newUserId` directly
validated_findings.trigger: Reading or maintaining testManageUserPermission: the refactored helper now takes a resource id String, yet the call constructs a full UserRepresentation via UserConfigBuilder only to immediately read back the same `newUserId` that is already in scope.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 168 shows 'UserConfigBuilder.create().id(newUserId).build().getId()' - this creates a UserRepresentation, sets its id to newUserId, builds it, then calls getId() which returns the same newUserId. This is pointless indirection; newUserId could be passed directly. The refactored helper takes a String id, making this builder usage unnecessary.

validated_findings.body: An extra admin REST call per invocation and inconsistent call style within the file (other migrated sites use `userAlice.getId()`), slowing tests slightly and confusing readers about whether the server fetch is intentional.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Redundant remote call and intra-file inconsistency introduced by the migration.
validated_findings.impact: An extra admin REST call per invocation and inconsistent call style within the file (other migrated sites use `userAlice.getId()`), slowing tests slightly and confusing readers about whether the server fetch is intentional.
validated_findings.root_cause: Mechanical refactor from the representation-based helper appended `.getId()` to the old representation-fetching expression instead of switching to the local accessor.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Replace `userAlice.admin().toRepresentation().getId()` with `userAlice.getId()`, matching the other migrated call sites.
validated_findings.title: Unnecessary REST round-trip via `userAlice.admin().toRepresentation().getId()` where `userAlice.getId()` suffices
validated_findings.trigger: Running testSingleUserPermission: the new id-based helper only needs the user id, but the call fetches the full UserRepresentation from the server via `admin().toRepresentation()` to obtain an id that `ManagedUser.getId()` already returns locally (as done at R107 and R222 in this same file).
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 86 shows 'userAlice.admin().toRepresentation().getId()' while ManagedUser.java line 20-22 shows getId() returns createdRepresentation.getId() directly. The admin().toRepresentation() makes an unnecessary REST call to fetch the full representation just to get the id that's already available locally via userAlice.getId().
